title: Q*Bert speech too slow: Votrax clock hardcoded to 720 kHz, speech-clock DAC unimplemented
description:
Q*Bert's Votrax SC-01 speech plays back noticeably slower than on real hardware.

## Root cause

The Gottlieb Rev 1 sound/speech board drives the Votrax SC-01's master clock with
a writable VCO controlled by a "speech clock DAC" mapped at 0x3000 on the sound
CPU. The game writes this DAC to set (and dynamically vary) the speech rate/pitch.

In phosphor this is unimplemented in two places:

- machines/src/gottlieb.rs:290-291 — the DAC write is a no-op stub:
      // Speech clock DAC: 0x3000-0x3FFF (stub — adjusts Votrax VCO)
      0x3000..=0x3FFF => {}
- machines/src/gottlieb.rs:92 — the Votrax master clock is hardcoded:
      const VOTRAX_CLOCK_HZ: u64 = 720_000;
  with a fixed divider 18/125 (gottlieb.rs:94-95, used at :144, :434, :889).

Because the DAC is ignored, the Votrax always runs at a fixed 720 kHz instead of
the rate the game requests, and the speech rate never varies.

## What MAME does

src/mame/shared/gottlieb_a.cpp:
- :419  convert_speech_clock(data) = 950000 + (data - 0xa0) * 5500
- :426  speech_clock_dac_w() -> m_votrax->set_unscaled_clock(convert_speech_clock(data))
- :438  the 0x3000 (mirror 0x0fff) write maps to speech_clock_dac_w
- :471  device is created with convert_speech_clock(0) as the initial clock

So the nominal clock (data=0xa0) is 950 kHz and the game adjusts it from there.
phosphor's fixed 720 kHz is ~76% of the 950 kHz nominal, i.e. speech runs roughly
24% too slow — consistent with the reported symptom — and the game's intended
pitch/rate variation is lost entirely.

## Fix sketch

1. Implement the 0x3000-0x3FFF write: compute clock = 950000 + (data - 0xa0)*5500
   and push it to the Votrax (add a set_clock/set_unscaled_clock on VotraxSc01 in
   core/src/device/votrax_sc01.rs that recomputes sclock/cclock from the new clock).
2. Make the gottlieb sound-board <-> votrax clock divider track the current Votrax
   clock instead of the fixed VOTRAX_CLOCK_NUM/DEN (18/125), since the divider
   ratio against the 5 MHz timebase changes with the DAC value.
3. Initialize the Votrax clock from convert_speech_clock(0) to match MAME's
   construction default.

## Verification

After the fix, compare Q*Bert speech rate against MAME (gottlieb1_votrax /
GOTTLIEB_SOUND_SPEECH_REV1A) — durations should match and pitch should vary as
the game writes the DAC.
close_reason: Implemented the speech-clock DAC (sound CPU 0x3000): it now retunes the Votrax SC-01 VCO via convert_speech_clock (950 kHz nominal at 0xA0, ±5.5 kHz/step), matching MAME. The board re-derives the Votrax tick divider and the device's internal sclock/cclock + resampler rate whenever the DAC changes (and after state load). Default clock raised from the incorrect fixed 720 kHz to the 950 kHz nominal, fixing the too-slow speech.

title: Mario Bros: no sound — 8049 sound engine never enables timer/interrupts
description:
Mario Bros (mariobros) graphics, inputs, DMA, NVRAM all work, but there is no sound; the DAC path itself is dead (not just the deferred discrete circuit).

Findings (verified with the real mariog ROM):
- The 8049 sound CPU runs but is stuck in its sample-playback loop at PC 0x900-0x9FF, continuously writing DAC=0x00. Audio is a constant -32768 (3 distinct values over 2.2M samples).
- It NEVER enables timer/counter/TCNTI/interrupt across a full run (EVER all 0), though the sound ROM has STRT T / EN TCNTI / EN I at 0x062/0x070/0x379/0x04d.
- The main Z80 DOES request sounds (47 nonzero cmd writes to 0x7e00, 102 nonzero triggers to 0x7f00-0x7f07), so the Mario-side wiring is fine; the 8049 just never processes them (its timer-interrupt dispatch never starts).
- 8049 boot immediately CALLs ROM bank 1 (0x100) via SEL MB/DBF. Suspect a bug in the shared phosphor-core I8035 8049-mode execution: DBF/SEL-MBx (A11) addressing on CALL/JMP, interrupt vectoring (ext 0x003 / timer 0x007), or the P2/tune_r MOVX bank-select. I8035 changes need cross-validation.
- Still deferred regardless: discrete walk/skid analog sound (nl_mario.cpp) + the 0x7f07 skid trigger.

Repro: run mariobros, coin+start into gameplay; DAC stays 0x00.
close_reason: Fixed in cebacf6. Root cause: the M58715 sound CPU has an undumped internal-ROM bootstrap that runs before the external program; per MAME's audiocpu trace it does ANL P2,#$DF; SEL MB0; CALL $101, entering the external program at 0x101 (STRT T). We started at external 0x000, where the STRT T at 0x101 is swallowed as the JC operand at 0x100, so the sound engine's duration timer never started and every effect hung in its playback loop with a silent DAC. MarioBrosSystem::reset now replicates the bootstrap (P2=0xDF, MB0, PC=0x101). DAC output went from 3 distinct values to 20k+ across the full range — digitized SFX now play. Verified by diffing our 8049 PC trace against MAME -debugscript. Discrete walk/skid analog sound remains deferred (separate).

title: Q*Bert MOB colors wrong: sprite bitplanes flipped vs MAME (LSB/MSB plane order)
description:
Q*Bert's motion-object (sprite/MOB) colors are wrong — the 4 sprite bitplanes
are flipped relative to MAME, permuting the 16 colors of every sprite by a
bit-reversal of the pen index. Same bug class as the Food Fight fix (commit
7978ad5): phosphor's decode_gfx orders plane_offsets LSB-first (entry 0 = pen
bit 0), the reverse of MAME's MSB-first planeoffset, so a machine that copies
MAME's plane list verbatim ends up with reversed planes.

Root cause — machines/src/gottlieb.rs, GottliebBoard::decode_gfx (~line 510):
    let planes: [usize; 4] = std::array::from_fn(|p| p * quarter * 8);
    // plane_offsets = [0, q*8, 2q*8, 3q*8]  (LSB-first: bit0 <- ROM quarter 0)

MAME (src/mame/gottlieb/gottlieb.cpp:2130 spr_layout):
    { RGN_FRAC(0,4), RGN_FRAC(1,4), RGN_FRAC(2,4), RGN_FRAC(3,4) }
    // MSB-first: planeoffset[0] = pen bit 3 <- ROM quarter 0

MAME maps bit3<-Q0, bit2<-Q1, bit1<-Q2, bit0<-Q3; phosphor maps bit0<-Q0 ...
bit3<-Q3 — every pen index p becomes bitrev4(p) (0<->0,1<->8,2<->4,3<->12,...),
scrambling each sprite's 16-color set.

Isolated to sprites: the tile layout in the same file (GOTTLIEB_TILE_LAYOUT,
plane_offsets [3,2,1,0]) IS correctly reversed vs MAME's gfx_8x8x4_packed_msb
(planeoffset {0,1,2,3} = STEP4(0,1), src/emu/video/generic.cpp:97), so tiles
render correctly. Sprite x_offsets/y_offsets/char_increment all match MAME
(STEP16(0,1)/STEP16(0,16)/32*8) — plane order is the only difference.

Scope: GottliebBoard::decode_gfx is used only by Q*Bert (machines/src/qbert.rs).
acceptance_criteria:
* Q*Bert MOBs (Q*Bert, Coily, balls, Slick/Sam, discs) render with MAME-matching
  colors; compare a screenshot to a MAME reference frame.
* Tile/playfield colors unchanged (already correct).
* cargo test -p phosphor-machines, clippy, and fmt pass.
close_reason: Fixed in 3ad18aa: reversed Q*Bert sprite plane order in GottliebBoard::decode_gfx to [3q,2q,q,0]*8 (LSB-first, matching MAME spr_layout's MSB-first planeoffset). Verified by user.

Follow-up polish from the Asteroids discrete-sound migration (l7o.3). See docs/debugging-asteroids-discrete-sound.md and tools/sound-reference/.

SYMPTOM
- By ear, thrust does not rumble enough, even though its band centre (~85 Hz) matches MAME's measured ~82 Hz peak / 128 Hz centroid. So it's not a pitch error — it's missing low-end weight/body.

HYPOTHESIS: MAME output post-processing
- MAME 0.287's new audio system applies a per-game <audio_effects> chain AFTER the discrete mix. ~/mame/cfg/asteroid.cfg shows: Filters, Compressor, Reverb, Equalizer on tag ':mono'. A compressor + low-shelf EQ would lift and thicken the sub-bass rumble in the *played* sound vs the raw netlist output.
- Open question: does '-wavwrite' tap the speaker mix BEFORE or AFTER that effects chain? If after, our captured 'ground truth' already includes the effects and Phosphor should match the post-effect sound. If before, the difference vs what the user hears is the effects chain.

INVESTIGATION
1. Capture MAME thrust with the audio_effects chain enabled vs disabled (clear/zero the effects in cfg, or a fresh cfg) and compare spectra — quantify how much low-end the compressor/EQ adds.
2. Determine the wavwrite tap point (pre/post effects) from MAME 0.287 source or by toggling effects and diffing captures.
3. Decide whether Phosphor should model an output-stage low-shelf/compressor (in the discrete framework's output stage, reusable across boards) to match the played sound, vs. matching only the raw netlist.

SECONDARY (from the case-study open threads)
- Consider wiring the Phosphor-vs-MAME centroid comparison (tools/sound-reference + machines/examples/asteroid_capture.rs) as a checked-in tolerance test, gated/local-only since it needs MAME + ROMs.

NON-GOAL: bit-exact audio. Target is matching the audible character (the deep thrust rumble) within tolerance.

title: Debug panel unsupported on 24-bit-bus (MC68000) machines
description:
The egui debug panel (F1 / --debug) is gated on MachineDebug::debug_bus() returning Some, and the debugger's memory inspector is 16-bit-addressed. The MC68000 machines (Food Fight, Quantum) run on a 24-bit AddressSpace32 bus and return None for debug_bus, so --debug silently does nothing for them (the frontend computes has_debug = machine.debug_bus().is_some() in frontend/src/emulator.rs and disables the panel).

Cycle/instruction stepping still works internally via MachineDebug::debug_tick; only the interactive panel (register view + memory inspector) is unavailable.

To support it, the debugger's BusDebug trait and the egui memory inspector / disassembly view in frontend/src/debug_ui.rs need to handle 32-bit addresses (currently u16-addressed). The #[derive(BusDebug)] macro and AddressSpace32 wiring would also need a 32-bit debug path.

Affects: foodf.rs, quantum.rs (both note this limitation in their MachineDebug impls).
close_reason: Debug panel now works on 24-bit-bus MC68000 machines. AddressSpace32 already had the full debug surface (debug_read/peek/poke/watchpoints, all u32) and the frontend memory viewer + disassembly were already u32-aware; the gap was that foodf/quantum exposed no BusDebug. Extended #[derive(BusDebug)] to infer address width from the map field type (AddressSpace16 vs AddressSpace32 — 32-bit routes addresses untruncated) and to expand #[debug_device] on [T; N] arrays into per-element entries; added AddressSpace32::debug_write parity wrapper. Wired foodf + quantum via derive + impl_standalone_debug!. memory_map() stays 16-bit-only (its return type is &AddressSpace16 and it's unused by the frontend, which reads via peek).

title: Discrete sound device framework (v1: Asteroids, Lunar Lander, Donkey Kong)
description:
Reusable framework for discrete / board-level analog sound paths, per docs/designs/discrete-sound-framework.md.

Replaces ad-hoc per-board discrete sound (currently: DkongDiscrete synthesizes finished 44.1kHz PCM and is mixed AFTER resampling, bypassing the board analog path; Asteroids and Lunar Lander discrete writes are stubbed under no_audio) with a typed Rust circuit graph: contiguous Vec<Node> enum + Node::Custom escape hatch, topo-sorted evaluation with one-step-delay back-edges for feedback, per-component clock domains, AudioResampler output, Saveable/Debuggable integration.

v1 scope = framework + three migrations. Order (Asteroids first to de-risk the framework on simpler latch/data-driven Atari boards before DK's harder shared-analog mixer):
  1. Framework skeleton + evaluation model
  2. Mixer and filter primitives
  3. Asteroids migration (first real consumer)
  4. Lunar Lander migration
  5. Donkey Kong migration

Follow-ons (DK Jr., Mario Bros., Asteroids Deluxe, Namco 54XX) are out of v1 scope and tracked separately.
close_reason: v1 complete. Built a reusable discrete-sound framework (core/src/device/discrete/: typed-handle builder -> DiscreteCircuit, Vec<Node> enum + Custom escape hatch, topo-sorted eval with one-step back-edges, per-component clock domains, mixer/filter primitives) and migrated all three v1 boards onto it, each verified against MAME 0.287 with a capture-and-compare rig (tools/sound-reference): Asteroids (l7o.3), Lunar Lander (l7o.4), Donkey Kong (l7o.5). The rig + case study (docs/debugging-asteroids-discrete-sound.md) caught multiple bugs ears missed (write_d7 latch, XNOR DC-lock, level/balance/headroom). Follow-ups tracked separately: hm4 (MAME output post-processing / thrust rumble); DK fidelity + DK Jr. reuse noted in l7o.5.

title: Discrete sound: framework skeleton + evaluation model
description:
Phase 1. Add core/src/device/discrete/.

- DiscreteCircuitBuilder + typed handles (LogicInputId/DataInputId/PulseInputId/ExternalSourceId/NodeId).
- DiscreteCircuit runtime: contiguous Vec<Node> enum over the v1 primitive set + a single Node::Custom(Box<dyn CustomComponent>) escape-hatch variant. Static dispatch for common primitives; box fat per-variant state.
- Evaluation model: topological sort at build(); per-node output-slot value array (Vec<f64>); cycle detection (DFS) cutting back-edges read with one-step delay; same held-slot mechanism provides cross-clock-domain sample-and-hold.
- DiscreteScheduler with per-component clock domains (BoardCycle / FixedFrequency / OutputSample / EventOnly); dt-based analog state.
- Basic input/source/math primitives (logic/data/pulse inputs, edge detector, fixed/variable square, LFSR noise, gain/add/multiply/clamp).
- AudioResampler integration to mono i16.
- Saveable: include node output slots (held + back-edge state); versioned.
- Unit tests for deterministic primitives (LFSR, square phase/freq, save/load round-trip).

No board migration in this phase.
close_reason: Implemented in core/src/device/discrete/ (mod.rs, node.rs, tests.rs): typed-handle builder -> DiscreteCircuit, Vec<Node> enum + Node::Custom escape hatch, topo-sorted evaluation with one-step-delay back-edges, per-component clock domains, input/source/math primitives + LFSR noise, AudioResampler<i16> output, versioned Saveable with node output slots. 14 unit tests pass; clippy + fmt clean.

title: Discrete sound: mixer and filter primitives
description:
Phase 2. Analog approximation primitives on top of the skeleton.

- RC charge/discharge (envelope), RC low-pass, RC high-pass / coupling cap.
- First-order and second-order filters (band-pass, Sallen-Key-style approximation).
- Resistor mixer (with optional pull-up/down/load), diode mixer (configurable forward drop/threshold), DAC / resistor ladder.
- External source input node (accept samples from existing chip/DAC devices).
- Per-primitive unit tests: RC approaches target within tolerance, filter step-response sanity, mixer scaling, diode threshold, DAC monotonicity/endpoints, external-source sample handling, save/load.
close_reason: Implemented analog primitives in core/src/device/discrete/: RC low-pass, RC high-pass/coupling, asymmetric RC envelope (charge/discharge), Chamberlin state-variable 2nd-order filter (low/band/high-pass), passive resistor mixer (weighted-average + optional load), diode-OR mixer (max minus forward drop), and R-2R/weighted DAC ladder. External-source node already present from skeleton; added builder methods, eval/reset/save-load, and FilterMode. 10 new unit tests (24 total in module); clippy + fmt clean.

title: Asteroids: migrate discrete sound to the framework (first consumer)
description:
Phase 3. First real migration — validates latch-driven + data-driven inputs and de-risks the framework before DK.

Add AsteroidsDiscreteSound (circuit + AsteroidsDiscreteInputs) and wire the currently-stubbed bus writes:
- 0x3600 explosion: bits 2-5 volume/data; bits 6-7 pitch divider (MAME-observed 00->12, 01->6, 10->3, 11->5 — verify against schematic).
- 0x3A00 thump: bit 4 enable; low nibble DAC data.
- 0x3C00..=0x3C07 addressable audio latch: saucer enable/fire/select, thrust, ship fire, life.
- 0x3E00 noise reset pulse.

Signal paths: thump DAC ladder->555/filter; saucer VCO/warble/filter; fire decay-square/filter; thrust LFSR->band/low-pass; explosion sampled-noise->RC; life 3kHz square -> output mix -> gain.

Remove no_audio from AsteroidsSystem; route AudioSource through the device. Saveable + Debuggable (SAUCER/THRUST/THUMP_DATA/EXPLODE_PITCH/NOISE_LFSR ...). Tests: mapping of each write, noise reset pulse, audio drains after a frame, save/load.
close_reason: Asteroids migrated to the discrete sound framework and verified against MAME 0.287 ground truth. Built machines/src/asteroids_sound.rs (AsteroidsDiscreteSound) modeling all 7 asteroid_a.cpp paths; wired bus writes 0x3600/0x3A00/0x3C00-07(write_d7)/0x3E00; replaced no_audio with a hand AudioSource; Saveable+Debuggable; ticked per frame. Added a triangle-wave primitive to the framework for the saucer. Built a MAME-capture-vs-Phosphor comparison rig (tools/sound-reference/ + machines/examples/asteroid_capture.rs) which caught two bugs the ear missed (explosion DC-locked on XNOR all-ones seed; thump 4x too high) — now every effect matches MAME within tolerance. Documented in docs/debugging-asteroids-discrete-sound.md. Remaining low-end-rumble polish tracked in phosphor-emulator-asteroids-sound-postprocessing-hm4. Tests/clippy/fmt green.

title: Lunar Lander: migrate discrete sound to the framework
description:
Phase 4. Compact register-driven circuit; reuses Atari noise/latch primitives established by the Asteroids migration.

Add LunarLanderDiscreteSound and wire stubs:
- 0x3C00 sound register: bits 0-2 thrust volume; bit 3 explosion enable; bit 4 3kHz tone enable; bit 5 6kHz tone enable.
- 0x3E00 noise reset pulse.

Circuit: 12kHz LFSR noise -> RC filter -> thrust gain (3-bit) -> band/low-pass; explosion gate; 3kHz and 6kHz fixed tones; final mix + output filter/gain.

Remove no_audio from LunarLanderSystem. Saveable + Debuggable. Tests: register mapping, noise reset, tone-only deterministic non-silent output, thrust/explosion non-silent, save/load.
close_reason: Lunar Lander migrated to the discrete sound framework and verified against MAME 0.287. New machines/src/llander_sound.rs (LunarLanderDiscreteSound) models MAME's llander_discrete netlist: a shared resettable 12kHz XNOR LFSR (Custom LanderNoise) -> RC LP -> band-passed thrust + unfiltered explosion (which reuses the 3-bit thrust value as its volume) -> 560Hz LP, plus fixed 3kHz/6kHz alert tones. Wired 0x3C00 sound register + 0x3E00 noise reset in llander.rs; replaced no_audio with a hand AudioSource; tick per frame; reset; Saveable+Debuggable; 5 tests. Extended the capture rig (drive_llander_sound.lua + llander_capture.rs + analyzer --llander); tuned gains to MAME's measured RMS balance (thrust 161~158, tones 21~21, explosion 1280~1712). Explosion's ~75% level + lower centroid is the same MAME output post-processing gap tracked in hm4. Tests/clippy/fmt green.

title: Donkey Kong: migrate DkongDiscrete to the framework
description:
Phase 5. Hardest migration: shared analog mixer + DAC-into-analog + discharge. Needs the diode/resistor mixers and DAC ladder from the primitives phase, plus a Node::Custom for DK's 555 control-voltage mixer.

Replace DkongDiscrete with DkongDiscreteSound:
- Tkg04Board::write_sound_control_bit feeds named circuit inputs (walk/jump/stomp).
- I8035 DAC writes feed the circuit DAC input; discharge/control lines feed inputs.
- Circuit owns stomp/jump/walk/DAC -> shared resistor mixer -> amp/filter -> resampler (replaces the current late post-resample PCM mix).
- Tkg04Board::fill_audio drains from the device.

Update TKG-04 audio, save-state, reset, and debug integration; preserve the frontend-facing machine API. Extend existing TKG-04 save-state tests. Debug registers: LATCH/WALK/JUMP/STOMP/DAC/DISCHARGE/MIX_OUT. (DK Jr. reuse is the cheap generalization check — share primitives, different topology.)
close_reason: Donkey Kong migrated to the discrete sound framework and verified against MAME 0.287 captures. New machines/src/dkong_sound.rs (DkongDiscreteSound): the I8035 DAC enters as an external source and is summed in-circuit with walk/jump/stomp (Custom components: 555 VCO + RC envelopes + LFSR), replacing the post-resample PCM add. Wired tkg04.rs (feed_dac steps the circuit per box-filtered DAC sample; write_sound_bit; fill_audio; save/load; reset; #[debug_device]); removed core DkongDiscrete. Built the MAME-vs-Phosphor comparison rig for DK (drive_dkong_sound.lua halts the Z80 to isolate the discrete effects; dkong_capture.rs; analyzer --dkong) — caught that the effects were ~135x too loud and ~5kHz too bright vs MAME. Fixed with per-effect 2nd-order low-passes (darken to MAME's ~300-1000Hz centroids) + MAME relative balance (walk subtle/jump/stomp prominent), and a DAC attenuation (~0.55, like MAME's VR2) to give output headroom so the effects are audible without clipping the full-scale music. User-confirmed audible. Tests/clippy/fmt green. FUTURE: faithful dkong2b_discrete (resistor/diode mixers, Sallen-Key DAC filter, discharge), an output soft-limiter (the hm4 post-fx thread), and DK Jr. reuse.

title: Missile Command: emulate + expose the R8 game-options DIP bank
description: Missile Command has two physical DIP banks: R10 (pricing, read at 0x4A00 — already exposed via DipSwitches as bank 0) and R8 (game options: Cities, Bonus City, Trackball Size, Bonus-credit-for-4-coins, Cabinet — read at 0x4000 via POKEY in MAME). Not a DipSwitches-trait limitation — the trait already supports multiple banks (see Tempest/DigDug/Galaga).

title: Galaxian/Scramble/Frogger arcade family
description:
Add the Galaxian -> Scramble -> Frogger hardware lineage to Phosphor (full family, both hardware tiers).

No new CPU required (Z80 exists); all sound chips already in-tree (Ay8910, i8255). The only genuinely new subsystem is the Galaxian-style video engine (tilemap + sprites + hardware starfield + bullet/shell RAM + PROM palette). Frogger is the requested anchor and lands on the more complex sound-CPU variant.

title: Rebuild Galaxian sound as a port of galaxian_discrete
description:
Rewrite core/src/device/galaxian_sound.rs build_circuit as a component-level port of MAME's galaxian_discrete (~/ws/mame/src/mame/galaxian/galaxian_a.cpp), using the new 555/op-amp primitives with the real GAL_R*/GAL_C* schematic values. Keep the register interface (pitch_w/lfo_freq_w/sound_w), input nodes, TuneVoice, and Device/Debuggable/Saveable impls. Voice mapping:
- Background/wolf-whistle: bg_dac -> dac_weighted(R18/17/16/15) -> ne555_cc(R21,C15 cap out) -> gain/add mult-add -> clamp(0,5) -> 3x ne555_astable FS1/2/3 (R22/R23/C17, R25/R26/C18, R28/R29/C19, gated by fs enables) -> resistor_mixer(R24/R27/R30,C20).
- Pitch/tune: keep TuneVoice.
- HIT: rc_disc5(noise, hit, R35+R36, C21) -> op_amp_band_pass([R35,R36], R37, C22, C23).
- FIRE: noise mix -> ne555_astable fire VCO (R44/R45/C27) -> rc_disc5(R41,C25).
- Final mix: pre-mixer (tune+bg, VOL1/VOL2 switched R49/R51/R50/R52/R34) -> resistor_mixer(R34/R40/R43, load R91) -> output ~32767/5.
Remove the approximation tuning (triangle FS, cascaded-LP hit, noise-FM fire) + the APPROXIMATION doc caveat. Keep the 10 existing device tests green. Validate end-to-end with the tools/sound-reference rig (analyze_wav.py --galaxian + spectrograms) against MAME and the recorded shot.wav/death.wav samples.
close_reason: Rewrote galaxian_sound build as a component-level port of MAME galaxian_discrete: R-1 DAC -> 555 CC wolf-whistle VCO -> 3 CV-modulated 555 astables; noise-gated op-amp band-pass HIT; noise-jittered 555 VCO + RCDISC5 FIRE; faithful two-stage resistor mix with C26/C46 coupling. Real GAL_R*/GAL_C* values. Also added op-amp rail clipping (faithful + bounds power-on transient) and out_high param to ne555_astable. 10 device tests + 34 primitive tests green.

description:

title: Discrete sound: faithful NE555 + op-amp primitives
description:
Add first-class, reusable analog primitives to core/src/device/discrete/ (node.rs + mod.rs), ported from MAME's BSD discrete core (~/ws/mame/src/devices/sound/disc_dev.hxx, disc_flt.hxx, discrete.h):
- Ne555Astable (with CV): port dsd_555_astable. Builder ne555_astable(name, cv_src, r1, r2, c, vcc, output). Precompute exp_charge=1-exp(-dt/((r1+r2)c)), exp_discharge=exp(-dt/(r2*c)) in the builder using self.sim_rate; state cap_v + flip_flop; CV modulates threshold/trigger. Square + Capacitor output modes. Drop MAME's sub-sample x_time loop (faithful at 192kHz sim rate; documented).
- Ne555Cc (constant-current VCO): port the simple type of dsd_555_cc; output capacitor voltage.
- OpAmpBandPass: port dst_op_amp_filt IS_BAND_PASS_1M + calculate_filter2_coefficients (biquad via pre-warped bilinear transform; fc/d/gain from r_in/rF/c1/c2). Precompute a1,a2,b0,b1,b2 in the builder from self.sim_rate.
- RcDisc5: port dst_rcdisc5 (gated diode RC discharge, 0.7V drop).
Follow the 6-step NodeKind pattern (enum variant, builder, eval, reset_runtime, save_runtime/load_runtime, deps). Reuse dac_weighted for R-1 DACs and gain/add/clamp for op-amp mult/add. Add per-primitive unit tests in discrete/tests.rs (555 oscillates near FREQ_OF_555=1.49/((R1+2R2)C); band-pass peaks near fc; rc_disc5 decays with tau=RC). No behavior change to existing devices. First commit of the 555/op-amp effort. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/plan-for-the-555-op-amp-resilient-abelson.md
close_reason: Added Ne555Astable, Ne555Cc, OpAmpBandPass, RcDisc5 NodeKind primitives (faithful ports of MAME dsd_555_astable/dsd_555_cc/dst_op_amp_filt IS_BAND_PASS_1M/dst_rcdisc5) with builder methods and 10 unit tests. No behavior change to existing devices.

Wire shared RAM, mathbox ROM banking (OUT0 bits4-1), statwr_w bit4 rising->run->FIRQ, status_r bit5. Accumulate cycles for realistic FIRQ delay. NOTE: existing core/src/device/mathbox.rs (Battlezone/Tempest fixed-function) CANNOT be reused.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: AM2901 microcoded mathbox. New core/device/irobot_mathbox.rs ports MAME's load_oproms+irmb_run (1024-op microcode decode, 8-function ALU, Q/shift destinations, jump/JSR/RTS sequencer, paged ROM/RAM/comm-RAM window). Wired into irobot machine: 0x2000-0x3FFF routed through the mathbox paging (out0), big-endian mathbox ROM assembled from 4 interleaved chips, statwr bit4 runs mathbox + FIRQ, status bit5 done. Save-state/reset cover the mathbox. 2 commits (device a0ae3ab, wiring 21327a2). 6 mathbox + 16 machine tests; full core (751) + machines (324) suites pass; clippy/fmt clean.

Save-state/reset cover the bitmaps + video latches. 5 new tests (draw_line, point + polygon rasterization via comm RAM, palette render, text-over-polygon compositing). 20 machine tests; core 751 + machines 329 pass; clippy/fmt clean. title: Marble Madness (Atari System 1)
description:
Add Marble Madness (1984), the project's first 16-bit multi-CPU arcade machine, on the Atari System 1 board (MC68010 main @ 7.15909 MHz + M6502 sound @ 1.789772 MHz).

Builds on the new M68000 core (first exercised by machines/src/foodf.rs, the closest end-to-end template). System 1 is the gateway to four more titles (Peter Packrat, Indiana Jones, Road Runner, RoadBlasters) that share this board.

User-chosen scope for this first cut:
- Audio: boot-first - POKEY only (reuse core/src/device/pokey.rs); YM2151 STUBBED (silent, but registers/IRQ wired so the sound CPU runs). Full FM synthesis is a tracked follow-up.
- Video: correct-but-staged - build the full alpha + playfield + motion-object compositor and palette first, then iterate the trickier PROM 4/5/6-bpp banking and SLIP scanline IRQs against MAME.

New components: Slapstic 137412-103 device, EEPROM 2804 (via Nvram), YM2151 stub, System 1 video (banked tilemaps + atarimo linked-list MO engine), machines/src/marble.rs.

Hardware verified against MAME atari/atarisy1.cpp, atarisy1_v.cpp, slapstic.cpp, atarimo.*.

Full plan: ~/.claude/plans/plan-for-marble-madness-goofy-rainbow.md

Verified the M68000 path is byte-for-byte unchanged (full cpu-validation incl. SingleStepTests passes; new 68010 tests added). Documented the deferred 68010 deltas (VBR, MOVEC/MOVES/RTD, MOVE from CCR, format $8 fault frame) in the README for Phase 1 to watch. 3 commits on branch marble-68010-fidelity.

title: Per-game settings: per-machine config overrides + unify DIP/binding persistence
description:
Make all config.toml settings overridable per game and restructure persistence so a machine's config overrides, DIP switch state, and input bindings live together under one per-machine section.

Today: config.toml (config.rs Config: rom_path, nvram_path, save_path, scale) is entirely global. state.toml (state.rs State) already persists input_bindings and dip_switches as separate top-level maps keyed by machine_id. So bindings + DIPs are per-game but config is not, and the three per-machine concerns are scattered.

Goal:
- Per-game config overrides for every Config field (rom_path, nvram_path, save_path, scale), keyed by machine_id. Resolution order: CLI arg > per-game override > global config.toml > built-in default. Global config.toml stays the user-edited default source.
- Restructure DIP + binding storage into a single per-machine settings section instead of separate top-level input_bindings / dip_switches maps. Sketch: State { window_position, machines: HashMap<String, MachineSettings> } where MachineSettings { scale, rom_path, nvram_path, save_path, dip_switches: Vec<u8>, input_bindings: Vec<SerializedBinding> } (all optional / diff-only — omit fields equal to the resolved default, drop the whole entry when empty, preserving the current no-redundant-defaults behavior).

MAME treats this port as 8 IPT_UNKNOWN switches for every MCR game — the coin/option meaning is interpreted by the SSIO sound ROM, with no documented per-bit layout — so the DipSwitches impl is currently left empty (see comment in satans_hollow.rs). To expose it: derive the MCR SSIO coinage scheme (operator manual / SSIO firmware analysis) and add a DipSwitchBank, or expose the 8 raw switches as a fallback.
